# Pettifer

## Overview

- **Age:** Elderly  <sub>[v2 c3 P22](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0022)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** J. A. Pettifer  <sub>[v2 c1 P1](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0001)</sub>; A crank  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

He is a low-statured, heavy-set man who is bald except for a small strip of hair encircling his ears. His round face turns violet when he becomes angry, revealing bulging blue eyes.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c1 P19](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0019)_

## Personality

Known as an eccentric and stingy crank in Brierley, he lives without fixed mealtimes or regular habits. He prides himself on being brutally candid and outspoken, often blurting out his thoughts without filter. Despite his short temper, crusty exterior, and argumentative nature, he possesses a soft spot for company, takes pleasure in being teased, and proves to be friendly and forgiving under the right circumstances.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025), [v2 c3 P42](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0042), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)_

## Traits

- Eccentric  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Stingy  <sub>[v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008)</sub>
- Candid and outspoken  <sub>[v2 c1 P15](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0015), [v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025)</sub>
- Touchy about his baldness  <sub>[v2 c1 P22](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0022)</sub>
- Short-tempered  <sub>[v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c2 P41](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0041)</sub>

## Abilities

- Making tea  <sub>[v2 c3 P34](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0034)</sub>

## Goals

- To keep his farm and grain protected from trespassing livestock  <sub>[v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013), [v2 c1 P15](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0015)</sub>

## History

After moving to Brierley, Mr. Pettifer acquired a reputation as an odd and miserly solitary farmer. Upon discovering Nell Harcourt's Jersey cow trespassing in his oat field multiple times, he confronted Nell in a fury, though her sharp retort about his baldness made him retreat. When Nell accidentally sold his cow to a cattle dealer believing it was her own, she visited him to confess and offered a homemade cake as an apology. Pleased with the cake and her honesty, Mr. Pettifer forgave the error and traded for Nell's cow instead, striking up a warm friendship with her. Later, during a severe thunderstorm, his kitchen chimney was struck by lightning, which killed his beloved parrot Nutmeg. Shortly thereafter, his estranged wife Emily tracked him down in Brierley after seeing an item in a newspaper, and the two reconciled and resumed living together.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013), [v2 c1 P21](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0021), [v2 c2 P37](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0037), [v2 c3 P23](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0023), [v2 c3 P30](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0030), [v2 c3 P46](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0046), [v2 c24 P43](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0043), [v2 c25 P15](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0015), [v2 c25 P49](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0049)_

## Background by volume

- Formerly lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, where his sister managed his housekeeping until her death.  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Promised his dying sister he would marry Emily Scott.  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Separated from his wife Emily after a feud exacerbated by his parrot's foul language, leading him to move to St. Brendan's Island.  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v2 c25 P58](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0058), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059)</sub>
- Purchased Robert Bell's farm in Brierley.  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Quotes

> Patience isn't a virtue anymore, miss.  <sub>[v2 c1 P13](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0013)</sub>

> I am merely a terribly candid old man . . . extremely prone to stating what is real, even when it happens to be somewhat direct.  <sub>[v2 c3 P25](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0025)</sub>

> I’m a crabbed, lonesome, crusty old chap, but I feel young again because of something about that little girl . . . and having that sensation repeated once in a while is something I’d like, since it’s so pleasant.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> In a town of this nature, a man truly requires a degree of defense, since he cannot engage in a checkers match with a neighbor without people alleging he desires to wed the sister of that neighbor and publishing the claim in the newspaper.  <sub>[v2 c25 P51](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0051)</sub>

> A couple of years is roughly sufficient time for circumstances to remain completely unchanged. Should they remain stationary for any greater duration, they could become covered in moss.  <sub>[v1 c30 P1](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0001)</sub>
